beliefs: f reverses each whitespace-separated word individually and inserts 'lmKA' immediately before the last word, with no space between lmKA and that word [E1, E2, E3, E4]
Runs of whitespace (spaces, tabs, newlines; leading, trailing, internal) collapse to single spaces in the output; all-whitespace input yields just 'lmKA' [E3, E4]
Single-word input (no whitespace) yields 'lmKA' + reverse(word) [E1, E2]
Trailing whitespace is dropped entirely (no trailing empty token); lmKA lands before the last real word, or at the end if only one word [E3, E4]
notes: Fixed the trailing-space case: 'a  ' should give 'a lmKA' (lmKA before the single word), not 'lmKAa'. Trailing whitespace is simply dropped, so the token list is the same as split().
